issues.title: Fifteen lowered upper bounds for n between 413 and 910: registration request
issues.author: JoostdeWinter
issues.body:
**Credit name.** Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology.

**Claim.** Fifteen upper bounds, each below the best value I could find in this repository at commit 200f2eb (all registered claims, with their monotonicity and border consequences).

| n | New side, rounded up | Best recorded value | Improvement |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 413 | 20.8239520077 | 20.8247640387 | 0.000812 |
| 494 | 22.7365988643 | 22.7375328752 | 0.000934 |
| 539 | 23.7365988643 | 23.7366696738 | 0.000071 |
| 543 | 23.8024287170 | 23.8030532611 | 0.000625 |
| 547 | 23.8787301198 | 23.8791276533 | 0.000398 |
| 590 | 24.8024287170 | 24.8025271329 | 0.000098 |
| 738 | 27.6912062515 | 27.6912836295 | 0.000077 |
| 739 | 27.6912835939 | 27.6914502721 | 0.000167 |
| 753 | 27.9026514302 | 27.9079842304 | 0.005333 |
| 794 | 28.6912835939 | 28.6914489810 | 0.000165 |
| 809 | 28.9079170470 | 28.9080360986 | 0.000119 |
| 810 | 28.9079170470 | 28.9104510455 | 0.002534 |
| 851 | 29.6912835939 | 29.6914489756 | 0.000165 |
| 867 | 29.9079170470 | 29.9080360977 | 0.000119 |
| 910 | 30.6912835939 | 30.6914489756 | 0.000165 |

**Certificate.** Exact rational certificates in the `.cert` format used for counts above 324 (first data line: n and the side, then centre x, centre y and t = tan(theta/2) per square). Repository https://github.com/JoostdeWinter/square-packing, folder `above324`, commit 71da0d56fd91b7061addca2a728ee72ec9728b0b.

**Checking.** `verify_cert.py` (Python standard library, `fractions.Fraction`): containment in the square and a separating-axis test on all pairs of squares with centres closer than sqrt(2). Command: `python3 -B verify_cert.py` in the folder `above324`. It checks all fifteen files in a few seconds. A second script with separate code checked the same packings in the same arithmetic before the files were written.

**What the checkers share.** One author, the separating-axis test, and Python's `Fraction`.

**Not done.** The certificates have not been replayed with the checkers of this project. The comparison covers this repository only. Public submission files of the Kaggle competition "Squares in Squares" contain smaller packings for 14 of these 15 counts (all except n = 543). For n = 413, 543 and 547 the side is less than 1e-43 above the local optimum of the arrangement, according to a numerical solution of the optimality conditions to 65 digits. This local optimality has no formal proof. For n = 494, 738, 739, 753 and 810 the certificate carries a margin of about 5e-9 above the numerical optimum.

**Lineage and credit.** The packings for n = 413, 494, 543, 547, 738, 739 and 810 are square sub-windows of Francisco Couzo's packings for n = 544, 539, 590, 696, 851, 851 and 868 (issue #763 and franciscouzo/square-packing at 43f666c). The packing for n = 753 is a sub-window of the n = 810 packing. Each sub-window holds more squares than the best recorded packing of the same side. The squares inside the sub-window were re-optimized locally, except at n = 547, where the sub-window was already at its local optimum. The packings for n = 539, 590, 794, 851, 867 and 910 add borders of axis-aligned squares to the packings for n = 494, 543, 739 and 810. The packing for n = 809 removes one square from the packing for n = 810. Credit for the source arrangements belongs to Francisco Couzo.

**AI assistance.** The sub-window search, local optimization, high-precision solution, rational certificates, checks and figures were produced with Claude (Anthropic) under my direction.

| 989 | 31.8889473785 | 31.8890306338 | 31.9096793514 | 8.3e-05 |

**Certificate.** Exact rational certificates in the `.cert` format used for counts above 324 (first data line: n and the side, then centre x, centre y and t = tan(theta/2) per square). Repository https://github.com/JoostdeWinter/square-packing, folder `above324_refined`, commit a9486ede74cd75996f488605f27d7fce32a73b3a.

**Checking.** `verify_cert.py` (Python standard library, `fractions.Fraction`): containment in the square and a separating-axis test on all pairs of squares with centres closer than sqrt(2). Command: `python3 -B verify_cert.py` in the folder `above324_refined`. It checks all sixteen files in a few seconds. A second script with separate code checked the same packings in the same arithmetic before the files were written.

**What the checkers share.** One author, the separating-axis test, and Python's `Fraction`.

**Not done.** The certificates have not been replayed with the checkers of this project. Each certificate carries a margin of about 5e-9 above the numerical optimum. The comparison with public competition packings covers the files I could find and may miss better private or newer packings.

**Lineage and credit.** The starting packings come from the file `data_out/best_certified_22.2226173_before_clearance.csv` in the repository Samanyu-dev/squares_in_squares at commit 53551d7. That file is a per-puzzle merge of public Kaggle notebooks and datasets for the competition "Squares in Squares". Its README credits Chris Deotte, lightningv08, alexchilton, kirilltym, malyshevdanil, prvsiyan, busyaprime, nilanjansaha123, jazivxt and the register of Francisco Couzo. The file does not name the author of each packing, so I cannot credit the sixteen arrangements individually. My contribution is a local re-optimization. All 1000 packings of the file were tested for a remaining descent direction with a linear program on the contact constraints. Sixteen still had one, and following the descent to convergence gave the values above. The arrangements of the squares are unchanged.

**AI assistance.** The descent test, local optimization, rational certificates and checks were produced with Claude (Anthropic) under my direction.
